blind_target.title: Two-digit comparison - Decomposed, holistic, or hybrid?
blind_target.evidence_quote: Regarding modulations of the numerical effects due to linguistic markedness of the task instruction, we expected to replicate the findings by Verguts and De Moor (2005) showing comparable distance effects for marked and unmarked task instructions.
blind_target.outcome_quote: However, in contrast to previous findings in single- and two-digit number comparison (Arend & Henik 2015; Verguts and De Moor, 2005), we did not detect reliable differences in overall response times in frequentist analyses. Although the Bayesian analysis supports the null model, the evidential value is relatively weak.
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: Distance invariance agrees (abstract and discussion report no numerical effect changes); expected overall latency contrast explicitly fails. No overall verdict for this target overrides the two comparisons.

blind_target.title: Choosing the larger versus choosing the smaller: Asymmetries in the size congruity effect.
blind_target.evidence_quote: In line with previous reports (Arend & Henik, 2015; Verguts & De Moor, 2005), we expected prolonged reaction times when instructed to pick the smaller as compared to picking the larger number.
blind_target.outcome_quote: However, in contrast to previous findings in single- and two-digit number comparison (Arend & Henik 2015; Verguts and De Moor, 2005), we did not detect reliable differences in overall response times in frequentist analyses.
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: Explicitly tests the prior overall reaction-time difference in a new number range; no difference found. Exploratory bin comparison also differs.
